newsitem.title: UK: NatWest set to overhaul markets arm - papers.
newsitem.headline: NatWest set to overhaul markets arm - papers.

text.p: National Westminster Bank Plc is planning to announce a major review of its business strategy which could lead to heavy cutbacks at NatWest Markets, its investment banking division, newspapers reported on Sunday.

Derek Wanless, NatWest's chief executive, was expected to signal the changes in 10 days' time when the bank releases the results of a three month investigation into how losses in its derivatives division mounted to 90 million pounds without being detected, The Sunday Times said.
"The changes follow a high-level rethink and are designed to calm the concerns of shareholders over the high cost of building up NatWest Markets (NWM)," The Sunday Times said.
The Sunday Telegraph said Martin Owen, chief executive of NWM was expected to resign when the report was published.

"Although he is under no pressure to resign from any of his fellow directors, the likely change in strategy at NatWest Markets is thought to have prompted his intention to leave," The Sunday Telegraph said.
In the past two years, Owen has led a major expansion at NWM and has masterminded a series of acquisitions including Gartmore, the fund manager, The Sunday Telegraph said.
The Sunday Times said Owen may decide to depart whether or not he is criticised in the report on the options losses.
Owen has said he would forgo 200,000 stg of his 1996 500,000 stg bonus as a result of the losses caused by mispricing of interest rate options.
The Bank of England and financial markets watchdog, the Securities and Futures Authority are scrutinising the affair.
The Sunday Times said the switch in strategy would signal a U-turn for the bank which had planned to turn NWM into one of the world's largest investment banks.
"Now it will openly declare itself a niche player, working only in markets where it can make profits," the Sunday Times said.
It said lending big sums to corporate customers where margins were wafer thin would be one casualty of the re-think, along with other areas where job losses would be almost inevitable.
But the businesses NWM has bought over the past two years would not be affected but would instead form the core of the slimmed-down NWM.
